newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent talked firmer after U.S. inventory data.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent talked firmer after U.S. inventory data.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Brent crude was firmer in early paper market talk on Wednesday as traders looked to overnight gains in the U.S. prompted by supportive inventory data.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said on Tuesday U.S. crude stocks fell by 5.9 million barrels last week as refineries ratcheted up gasoline production ahead of the start of the peak driving season.
IPE July Brent was trading at $20.10 a barrel by 1010 GMT, 10 cents above its settlement and much firmer than late partial cargo deals on the 15-day cash market as low as $19.90 a barrel.

Dealers said intermonth cash Brent spreads were also holding late Tuesday gains in thin talk, with June/July edging into narrow backwardation at +2/+4 cents. July/August was pegged at -5/-1 cents with Aug/Sep valued flat.
Brent CFDs were steady to firmer, the balance of this week and May 27-30 dates talked at July Brent -15/-10 cents.

Dated Brent traded twice on Tuesday -- at July -25 cents for a million late May barrels and July -10 cents for a June 4-6 cargo. Traders said the benchmark grade should hold the upper end of the range with a U.S. refiner expected to pick up another cargo to fill a VLCC sailing trans-Atlantic.
Two June 5-7 Brent cargoes were due to be nominated from the paper chains on Wednesday but one of them was thought committed to the equity holder's system.
Other North Sea markets got off to a slow start, extending Tuesday's stalemate as refinery buyers struggling with thin product margins showed a reluctance to meet sellers' higher offers.
